title: THE POT THAT MUST BE BROKEN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The clay pot the meat is cooked in must be broken; but if it is cooked in a bronze pot, the pot is to be scoured and rinsed with water."'" - Lev 6:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two vessels, two different treatments. Clay is porous — it absorbs. Once the sin offering had been cooked in it, that pot could never be fully cleaned. It had to be smashed. Bronze is non-porous, so scouring and rinsing was enough.

The instruction is practical, but it teaches something real about how sin works.

Some things in our lives can be scrubbed and returned to use. Others have absorbed too much and need to be broken and let go of entirely. A friendship, a habit, a source of entertainment, a business arrangement — sometimes the answer is careful adjustment, and sometimes the answer is ending it.

We usually prefer scouring. Breaking feels extreme.

But Jesus used far stronger language than a clay pot: If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away (Mtt 5:30). He was not commanding self-harm; He was insisting that some things are worth losing entirely rather than keeping and being ruined by. The believers at Ephesus understood this and publicly burned their sorcery scrolls, at enormous financial cost (Acts 19:19).

Wisdom is knowing which pot you are holding. Some things need cleaning. Some need breaking.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something in my life I keep scouring when it actually needs breaking?
2. What am I afraid of losing if I let it go?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me wisdom to know what can be cleaned and what must be let go. Give me courage to break what needs breaking. Amen.
